questions.question: Pointer variable is used to hold the _________ of the variable.
Which among the given operators is referred to as 'address of' operator?
Which among the given statements is incorrect?

options.text: Use of return statement is necessary in every function
Return statement may not be followed by a parenthesis
A program may contain more than one return statement
Return statement may not return a value

questions.explanation: A void method, constructor, or iterator does not need a return statement. A method may have several return statements, return; is valid in a void method, and parentheses around the returned value are optional.

questions.question: What is the size of a char in C#?
questions.explanation: sizeof(char) is 2 because a C# char is a UTF-16 code unit. sizeof(char*) is 4 or 8 depending on the process (32-bit vs 64-bit), not 2.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code segment?

options.text: Output is the address contained in p

questions.explanation: A void* may hold the address of an unmanaged value, but C# does not allow dereferencing it. *p is a compile-time error (CS0242); cast to a typed pointer first, for example *((int*)p).

questions.question: Which among the following is referred as an array of pointers?
questions.explanation: int*[] is an array of pointers. C# does not allow a size in the type (int*[4] p is a compile error). int* p is one pointer; int p[4] is not valid C# array syntax.
